In my case, it was my left knee having a pain after running, as in go run a 10k, get home, sit down for 20-30 min, stand up, fall over with locked knee swearing.

We found that my left glute and VMO (inner quad) were not firing/weaker than on t he right side...this lead to the outer quad and the connective tissue taking up an assload of strain to stop my knee caving in on every stride

So lots of, clamshells, glute bridges, banded side stepping for hip abduction, peterson step ups, single leg press, single leg extension (working in the top 15 degrees) and squats later not only did I end up putting more perk in my butt and building some sick wheels we also fixed the knee issue.

It depends on what makes your knees bad (the above will do jack for blown out miniscus/cartilidge for example) but if there is no history of direct trauma to the knee then it is worth looking into exercises that strengthen the musculature of the hip/glutes as these play a major part in walking/running and are somewhat neglected these days due to how much sitting down we do compared to 30 years ago.
